title: A Log That Tells You What Went Wrong: Reading a Field Run for Stuck, Slipping, Off the Path, Draining and Missing Time

questions.question: Why is the span of a finding marked from the start of its window?
options: So that every span is at least three seconds long
The window needs time to see the fault, so the span would start late
Because the rows are stored in windows
To line the spans up with whole seconds
questions.explanation: A stuck vehicle is only known to be stuck after three seconds of not moving. Marking every row of the window puts the start where the fault began.

questions.question: In the run with five faults, how many were found?
questions.explanation: Stuck, slipping, off the path, draining and a gap were put in at known times, and each was found within 1.8 s of its true start and end.

questions.question: Twenty clean runs with noise gave how many false findings?
questions.explanation: Marks closer than a second are joined and spans shorter than 2 s are dropped, which is what keeps noise from being reported.

questions.question: A slip that left the ground at 80 percent of the wheels was:
options: Not reported: the threshold is 70 percent
questions.explanation: The test is ground speed under 70 percent of wheel speed. 80 percent is over the line and 50 percent was reported.

questions.question: Where does the ground speed come from, when judging slip?
questions.explanation: Slip is the wheels saying one thing and the ground another. The ground's side has to come from somewhere other than the wheels.

questions.question: Why is a gap a finding?
options: It makes the file hard to read
The other tests say nothing about the time that is missing
It shows the battery was low
It always means the vehicle was switched off
questions.explanation: With 20 s of rows gone nobody knows what happened in them. The other four tests are silent about that time, so the gap is reported by itself.
